question.problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane

$$
r=⟨3,-2,1⟩+t⟨2,-5,1⟩+s⟨3,-6,0⟩,\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
question.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $v=⟨2,-5,1⟩$ and $w=⟨3,-6,0⟩$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $v$ and $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -6 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & -5 & 1 \\ 3 & -6 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =6i+3j+3k \\  & =⟨6,3,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨6,3,3⟩.$
